{{Quote|Suburban bliss and tranquility Liberty City style. Home to many of Liberty City's more affluent gangsters, Liberty City's commuter-belt is a patchwork of swimming pools, picket fences, backyards, basketball nets, street gangs and 5 car garages. It is littered with ostentatious mansions paid for in blood money, protected by high security guards and gates to keep out the gangs of bored teenagers looking for something to do to bring some excitement to their middle class existence. The designer dogs and the station wagons give a shallow serenity to suburbia but don't be fooled, violence and corruption are at the heart of every home.|''Grand Theft Auto III'' Manual, p. 6}}
'''Shoreside Vale''' is a borough in [[Liberty City (3D Universe)|Liberty City]] in {{III}}, {{A}} and {{LCS}}. It is the third and last borough the player encounters in all the three {{3D}} games based in Liberty City.

==Description==
Shoreside Vale is primarily residential, but also features the [[Francis International Airport (3D Universe)|Francis International Airport]] to the south, a light commercial and industrial estate ([[Pike Creek]]) on the western edge, and the [[Cochrane Dam]] in the northwestern corner. Shoreside Vale is the only part of the city situated on the mainland and is considerably hillier than the other two boroughs, with a mountain range along the northern edge of the borough.

With steep elevation changes, a river dividing the main residential area from the industrial estate and the airport, and roads, bridges and tunnels criss-crossing each other at different elevations, Shoreside Vale is notoriously tricky to navigate. For this reason, Shoreside Vale is a very poor choice for the [[Vehicle Missions|vehicle missions]].

Shoreside Vale was internally named as the 'Suburban' area during development, and, according to beta maps, the southern part of Shoreside Vale was going to consist of roads and possibly more suburbs, until the airport was moved towards Shoreside Vale instead. It is mainly based on the various suburbs in Weschester County in Upstate New York, the Bronx, and parts of north-east New Jersey.

==Neighborhoods, Districts and Areas==
===Cedar Grove===
[[Cedar Grove]] is an upper-class residential neighborhood which takes its name directly from a New Jersey suburb. It is based on White Plains, New York and Cedar Grove New Jersey. It is controlled by the [[Colombian Cartel]], and is home to some of the more wealthy residents of Liberty City. It consists of lavish mansions with swimming pools and fast sports cars on the drive-ways. [[Donald Love]]'s [[Cartel Mansion|mansion]] (later taken over by [[Catalina]] and the Colombian Cartel) and one of [[Toni Cipriani]]'s [[Shoreside Vale Safehouse (GTA LCS)|safehouses]] in [[Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories]] also lie within this area.

The [[Upstate Tunnel|tunnel]] that leads from one side of Cedar Grove to the other seems to have another road that leads to another part of Liberty City. The tunnel is unavailable to the player in ''GTA III'', but in ''GTA Liberty City Stories'' the player is allowed to use it to get to points around Cedar Grove. There seems to be another road that leads to a northern part of Shoreside Vale, but is blocked off and cannot be driven on. The sign above the road reads "[[Upstate Liberty (3D Universe)|Upstate]]". Rockstar stated there was never meant to be anything on the other side of the tunnel, but was used to give the player a feeling that Liberty City was larger than just the areas the player could explore{{Ref|name=upstatetunnel|type=rockstarweb|ref=http://www.rockstargames.com/newswire/article/19981/grand-theft-auto-iii-your-questions-answered-part-two-911-the-gh.html}}. In ''GTA III'' the player can fly a [[Dodo (3D Universe)|Dodo]] around the "upstate" part of Liberty City and will only find more hills. It could possibly be outside Liberty City since the maps of Shoreside Vale show it is part of the mainland.

===Francis International Airport===
[[Francis International Airport (3D Universe)|Francis International Airport]] is Liberty City's airport is situated on the southern half of Shoreside Vale, just off the main road coming into the area. Other features in this district include a long-term parking lot, a [[Liberty City Fire Department (3D Universe)|fire station]], a [[Subway in GTA III|subway]] [[Shoreside Terminal LCS|station]] and a [[Police Car|police car]] parked. There is a lot of airplanes and helicopters around the airport, however, none of them are accessible, with exception of the Dodo.

===Pike Creek===
[[Pike Creek]] is a light commercial and industrial district located in the western section of Shoreside Vale and is very similar to industrial areas on the outskirts of Yonkers, New York and Newark, New Jersey. It is home to the offices of several businesses, including [[Punk Noodles]], [[Turtle Head Fishing Co.]], [[AMCo. Petroleum Company]], and [[Liberty Pharmaceuticals]]. Services include the local police station, the [[Hope Medical College|hospital]], [[Pay 'n' Spray]] and [[8-Ball|8-Ball's]] [[8-Ball Autos|bomb shop]]. Pike Creek is [[Yakuza (3D Universe)|Yakuza]] turf in [[1998]], but is occupied by no gang in [[2001]], the setting [[Grand Theft Auto III]] (although it does have Yakuza presence during [[Bait|one mission]]).

===Wichita Gardens===
[[Wichita Gardens]] is a low-wealth residential neighborhood, mainly composed of Section 8 housing projects, like common neighborhoods In Yonkers and The Bronx in which it is mostly based on. It was formerly controlled by the [[Forelli Crime Family]], but it is now controlled by the [[Southside Hoods]], thanks to Toni Cipriani's [[Rough Justice|help]]. It is also home to [[Shoreside Vale Safehouse (GTA III)|one]] of [[Claude]]'s [[North West Towers|safehouses]].

==Trivia==
*In ''[[Bully]]'', another game made by [[Rockstar Games]], there is an area called {{Bully|Old Bullworth Vale}}, which resembles the [[Cedar Grove]] area of Shoreside, both being high society areas where the rich citizens of both cities live.
*In {{LCS}}, the player can get a (very) limited preview of Shoreside Vale before unlocking it by taking the [[Subway in GTA III|subway]] and getting off at the [[Shoreside Terminal LCS|airport station]] (the player can walk about the station, but the staircase outside is blocked). Using the [[Cheats in GTA Liberty City Stories|cheat]] that allows vehicles to drive on [[water]], it is possible to explore Shoreside Vale before it is unlocked. Similarly, at the cost of failing the mission, it is possible to enter Shoreside Vale during the [[Shoot the Messenger]] mission using the [[Speeder (boat)|boat]] supplied for the mission (although this is only possible for a brief time before the mission fails on its own). However, in Shoot the Messenger, if the player kills the driver of the targetted boat with a [[Sniper Rifles|sniper]], while having their given boat, the player can explore Shoreside Vale without any limitations.
*In ''GTA Liberty City Stories'', the map of Shoreside Vale is not the same as in {{III}}; a big portion of a mountain layer in the right part is missing, being replaced by an empty space. Oddly, in gameplay, the mountains still exist in the same portion where the mountain layer is missing from the map.
*There are no gun shops in Shoreside Vale in ''GTA III'' and ''GTA Liberty City Stories''. However in ''GTA III'', [[flamethrower]]s and [[Molotov Cocktails|molotovs]] can be bought from the [[Pike Creek LCPD Compound]]. In {{A}}, an [[Ammu-Nation (3D Universe)|Ammu-Nation]] is located at the depot which is later used as the [[Turtle Head Fishing Company Packaging Plant]].
*The [[Ghost Town|mocap cutscene scenery]] created specifically for the [[Introduction (GTA III)|bank robbery]] introduction [[Cutscenes|cutscene]] in ''Grand Theft Auto III'' is located behind the [[Cedar Ridge]] hills, only being accessible via exploits. In {{TDE}}, the assets used in the cutscene are set to despawn permanently after the cutscene ends.
*In ''Grand Theft Auto III - The Definitive Edition'', low-poly houses, street props and static boats are placed in the mountains, depicting an unseen residential area. This area only serves as background scenery, non-[[canon]]ically replacing the empty hills of the original versions.
